summary: Iter-32/33 — Org Ownership Transfer Flow. Backend FULLY VERIFIED: 16/16 pytest cases pass (status machine, plan-tier gate 402, accept/decline/cancel, 403/400 guards, also_leave scrub, idempotency). Frontend mostly works (Transfer button on MemberRow, OwnershipTransferModal, OutgoingTransfersPanel, PendingTransfersBanner, Decline + Accept happy path all render). ONE CRITICAL FRONTEND BUG found: the 402 inline upgrade CTA (transfer-upgrade-{id} + transfer-upgrade-cta-{id}) never surfaces because the global axios response interceptor in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js stringifies the structured FastAPI HTTPException detail dict before PendingTransfersBanner.accept() can read detail.code='plan_upgrade_required'.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking Accept on a transfer when recipient's plan is insufficient does NOT surface the inline upgrade card (data-testid='transfer-upgrade-{id}'). Backend correctly returns HTTP 402 with detail={code:'plan_upgrade_required', required_tier, current_tier, message}, but the axios response interceptor at /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js:215-224 unconditionally rewrites any object-typed `err.response.data.detail` to a flat string via errorMessage(). By the time PendingTransfersBanner's catch block runs, `detail` is a string, so the `typeof detail === 'object' && detail.code === 'plan_upgrade_required'` check fails. Result: only the generic toast appears, no upgrade button is shown. User has no way to navigate to /app/billing?subscribe={tier} from the banner.

action_items: FIX (high): /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js response interceptor (lines 215-224) currently stringifies ALL object-typed detail payloads. This breaks structured 402 responses with detail.code. Recommended fix: only stringify Pydantic validation arrays (Array.isArray(d)) — leave object dicts as-is. Optionally, attach raw object at err.response.data._rawDetail before mutation so callers can opt in. After the fix, PendingTransfersBanner will surface the upgrade CTA and the navigation to /app/billing?subscribe={tier} will work as specced.

Investigate: ensure the same interceptor change does NOT regress other call sites that rely on `detail` already being a string (search for `response.data.detail` across /app/frontend/src — there are ~30 hits; most pass it to toast.error which handles both).
critical_code_review_comments: org_transfers.py is clean: pure factory pattern, no circular import, atomic role mutation order (recipient first, outgoing last, transfer-accept last) leaves system in a recoverable state if any step throws.
org_transfers.py _required_tier_for_member_count: hardcoded thresholds duplicate billing.py PLANS. Acceptable per the inline comment, but mark as a known drift risk if PLANS changes.
org_transfers.py accept: lazy expiry check works (returns 410 with 'expired' message), good UX.
org_transfers.py: also_leave_after team scrub uses $pull on member_user_ids + admin_user_ids — wrapped in try/except so partial scrub doesn't block the transfer.

api.js interceptor (lines 215-224) is too aggressive — see action item above. The docstring says the goal is to flatten Pydantic validation ARRAYS (which it does at line 219 first half), but the same line also catches arbitrary object detail payloads, which silently breaks any endpoint that returns structured business-error detail dicts. The 402 transfer endpoint is the first known victim. Future endpoints that return detail.code patterns will hit the same trap.
PendingTransfersBanner.js: decline uses native window.confirm() — fine for desktop, but should consider a styled modal for mobile parity.
OrgPage.js MemberRow Transfer button: gated on isOwner + member.user_id !== meId — correct.

rca of the issue: Root cause of 402 upgrade-CTA not rendering: axios response interceptor at /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js:215-224 was authored to flatten Pydantic validation errors (arrays of {loc,msg,...} objects) into a single string. The condition `(d && typeof d === 'object' && !Array.isArray(d))` was added to also catch single-object validation errors, but it inadvertently catches ALL non-string detail payloads — including FastAPI HTTPException(detail={...}) responses that callers EXPECT to read as structured objects. Reproduction: as recipient on spark plan, accept a transfer in an org with 2+ members → backend returns 402 with detail={code:'plan_upgrade_required', required_tier:'temper', ...}. Network tab shows the correct response; React state never receives the dict (interceptor mutated it to a string before catch ran). Mitigation: narrow the interceptor's mutation to ONLY Array.isArray(d) (the actual Pydantic case). Object-typed details are already React-safe IF callers use them properly; toast.error sites that bypass errorMessage() are the historical concern, but those can be patched individually instead of breaking object detail for everyone.
